This schedule applies to all spaces; any single space can switch it off or pick a different delegate under Space settings → Delegate here.

about.step1: Real employees register with an email address; in development the verification link shows up right in the in-app inbox, and once an SMTP relay is connected the mail is really sent.
about.step2: Each virtual employee brings its own OpenAI-compatible base URL and a separate API key; keys are stored AES-GCM-encrypted, and neither the API nor the browser ever sees the plaintext. To try the flow first, use the built-in {0} demo endpoint.
about.step3: Every space has a UUID: with it you can request to join (the owner or an admin approves), or you can accept email invites only; admins can add and remove members, and the owner can transfer ownership or promote admins.
about.step4: @-mentioning a virtual employee in a space drops a task into their mailbox; @-mentioning a real employee sends a notification through the channel they chose (virtual or real email).
about.step5: If a person has set a delegate schedule in Settings, an @ aimed at them also drops a task for that virtual employee under their name, who answers under its own signature with an "answering for @X" tag on the bubble; the notification still goes to the person — answering for someone is not receiving for them. The schedule applies to every space; a single space can turn it off or pick another delegate in its settings, and whether it is active is judged by the clock at the moment of dispatch.
about.step6: Virtual employees pick up mail FIFO; across spaces their time is sliced by weight (evenly by default, weights confirmed by the owner/admin in the member panel), and each tick allocates slots with the largest-remainder method. One (employee, space) pair runs at most one task at a time; a new @ during a reply interrupts the running output and re-runs it as an interjection.
about.step7: Memory has two tiers: the employee's own common memory and a per-stream memory for each space. When a window exceeds its budget it is compressed, per space, into one summary memory that records the message numbers it covers; older history is retrieved back through MCP.
about.step8: MCP has two layers: the internal tool loop an employee runs during a task (search_history / read_window / list_files / read_file / get_context), and an outward JSON-RPC endpoint accessed with a space key generated by the owner. When delivering, the employee marks this space's files as that round's deliverables; a delivery card appears under the reply and opens a preview of the original.
about.step9: You can register several work VMs and authorize them per space, and a new space can bind one at creation; the edge functions have no TCP sockets, so the server only probes port reachability — your interactive console goes from the browser straight to a gateway on the machine, while employee-side execution still waits on a runner.
about.runtimeDesc: These come from the server right now, not canned text.
about.boundaryNotice: Boundary note: the database tables are open to the site's Function for reads and writes, and permissions are decided at the function layer per session; if any path bypasses the site and talks to the database directly, application-layer authorization no longer holds, and this boundary has not been penetration-tested in a deployed environment. Virtual employees' keys and VM credentials are stored encrypted and decrypted only in use.

plugin.bundledHint: These plugins ship inside the site; the manifest is the submission format — download or copy one to start from a working example.
plugin.guideTitle: How to write a plugin and submit it to the Market
plugin.guideStep1: Write the module: registerMessageRenderer declares id, priority, match and render; render returns React elements only — never innerHTML.
plugin.guideStep2: Write the manifest at plugins/bundled/<id>/manifest.json: schema, id, kind, version, entry and integrity, where integrity is the sha256 of the entry file in SRI form.
plugin.guideStep3: Submit: open a PR against plugins/bundled/ in this repository; a separate workstream-plugin-<id> repo also needs a copy bundled here.
plugin.guideStep4: Acceptance: npm run check:schema reconciles the manifest, the catalog and the entry file hash — if the three disagree the change cannot merge.

plugin.tipsTitle: Three things to know before using plugins
plugin.tip1: 1. Plugin tool names and descriptions go into the model context verbatim — that is feeding external copy to your employees. Only connect sources you trust.
plugin.tip2: 2. Tools are account-wide: connect once and every virtual employee under your account can call them in any group; to keep one employee off them, disable this connector.
plugin.tipLimits: 3. The limit is {limit} connectors per person, up to 24 tools each; calls time out after 60 seconds, and replies over 512KB fail outright instead of dragging down the whole turn.
plugin.tipCatalog: Ready-made MCP services are listed in the {0}; WorkStream does not redistribute them — you connect the service itself.
step.errToolUnknown: This tool name isn't on this turn's list — the model made it up, so nothing ran.
step.errConnectorToolUnmatched: This external tool is no longer among the connectors the owner has enabled (disabled or removed), so nothing ran.
step.errConnectorNeedsRun: Connector tools can only be called in the turn where an agent takes the mail; other paths reject them.
step.errInvalidArguments: The arguments aren't valid JSON, so they were never handed to the tool.
step.errInterrupted: Someone spoke up in the stream, so this turn was cut off.
step.errSliceInterrupted: The time slice ended before this step closed, so it was reclaimed.
step.errStepUnfinished: This step was still open when the whole mail wrapped up.
step.errStepWriteFailed: This step couldn't be written to the store.
step.errSummaryEmpty: Upstream returned an empty body, so this batch wasn't folded into the summary; the watermark didn't move and the next over-budget pass will try again.
step.pickHint: Click a note to see that turn's chain of thought, tool arguments and result; drag to select a stretch of time.
step.chatPrivacyNote: None of this shows in the chat — it lives only in this mail's trajectory; the thread still carries just the final reply.
step.slotsHeader: Prompt slots · {stable} chars reused in steady state / {volatile} rewritten each turn
step.slotVolatileTitle: Rewritten every turn from here on — the provider's prefix cache ends at this block
step.contextNote: This records the measure, not the text: the transcript can already be read in the stream, and a second copy would only bloat the store. The slot row shows which blocks this turn's system prompt was built from — the provider can reuse everything before the breakpoint verbatim, so when the hit rate drops, check which block moved.
step.timingNote: Throughput is output tokens ÷ the time after the first token; the cache hit comes from the usage upstream reports — when the endpoint reports nothing, it shows as “—”.
step.clippedNote: {original} characters in full; the store keeps only the first {kept} for a single step.
step.schemaNote: {0} — the input declaration from the same tool list as the arguments actually passed.
step.noSchemaNote: This step has no matching tool declaration — most likely a tool name the model invented.

scheduler.intro: Each virtual agent pulls mail FIFO from its own inbox; time slices across streams are split by weight. No real-time preemption—a running task finishes before it yields.
scheduler.noAgents: No one to schedule yet: create a virtual agent and put them in at least one stream.
scheduler.shareHint: Shares are cut from the per-tick budget using the largest-remainder method; to change a weight, the stream owner or an admin confirms it in the stream's Members panel.
scheduler.workersHint: Standalone worker processes claim turns against the same database; they keep working while the control plane upgrades, and a node whose heartbeat stops gets reclaimed.
scheduler.workersEmpty: No standalone execution workers registered yet: progress is driven by the embedded scheduler or frontend polling.
scheduler.cronLimitHint: Due times are computed on the server clock, not by card-flipping: up to {max} schedules per person, minimum interval {min} minutes. Due points that pile up while offline deliver as one mail and the rest count toward "merged"; points missed during a pause aren't made up—resuming starts from the first due point after now.
scheduler.draftPausedHint: This schedule is currently paused: saving changes keeps it paused—press "Resume" to let it run again.
scheduler.purposeHint: Can't be changed after creation: switching modes would silently change what this schedule means—delete and recreate instead.
scheduler.purposeWork: Work when due (speak in the stream)
scheduler.purposeDream: Merge global memory when due (not posted in stream)
scheduler.agentHint: Only virtual agents under your own name can be scheduled: borrowing someone else's agent burns their API key.
scheduler.streamHint: Only streams where both you and this agent are members.
scheduler.noSharedStream: This agent isn't in any stream shared with you
scheduler.intervalHint: Between {min} and {max} minutes. Changing the interval re-anchors the clock to the next due point.
scheduler.atHint: This wall-clock time is read with the timezone offset below.
scheduler.instructionHintDream: For a merge round the material is the compressed summaries of your streams; this line is only an extra note (e.g. "merge only to-dos and numbers") and may stay empty.
scheduler.instructionHintWork: When it wakes, the agent sees this instruction plus the stream's recent transcript. It can't be empty; if it should stay quiet when there's nothing to do, write that into this line.
scheduler.instructionPlaceholderDream: Merge only stable facts and open to-dos; copy names and numbers verbatim.
scheduler.instructionPlaceholderWork: Check live alerts and report anything urgent; stay quiet if there's nothing urgent.
scheduler.noCron: No schedules yet: give one of your agents a standing task, and it will speak up in the stream when due—no mention needed.
scheduler.dreamStreamNote: (only where the mail lands; this round won't post in the stream)
scheduler.dreamNoInstruction: (no extra note this time; merged by default rules)
scheduler.agentPausedWarn: This agent is currently paused; the next due round will fail outright.
scheduler.cronFooter: When due, its round queues behind real mentions: if a human is waiting for an answer, people first—missed due points still catch up on the clock next round. If the agent leaves the stream, this schedule pauses itself and the UI shows it honestly as paused; only its owner can re-schedule it. Global-memory merges never post in the stream—they only fold each stream's summary into the memory below.
scheduler.dreamIntro: Merges the compressed summaries of all your streams into one "about you" digest. It rides in every prompt but only guides how to answer—being cross-stream, it's never read out to the current stream. Three entry points: merge when a stream collapses history (the switch below), merge on a schedule (create a "merge global memory" schedule above; {n} now), or run it here manually.
scheduler.dreamAutoLabel: Merge right after a stream compresses
scheduler.dreamAutoHint: Rounds with nothing new cost no model calls; it just waits for the next stream's material.
scheduler.dreamAgentHint: Only borrows its model and key for this run; the result belongs to you, not the agent.
scheduler.dreamStreamHint: The mail must land in some agent's stream inbox to queue; the merge itself never posts.
scheduler.dreamEmpty: No global memory yet: get your agents running in streams first—merging needs each stream's compressed summaries.
staff.intro: Pick a role template and create an employee from it: name, responsibilities and system prompt are filled in together, and you land on the detail page to add a key or switch the model.
staff.noServer: No deployment server is registered yet: try the flow on the demo endpoint, or register one on the Virtual staff page.
staff.reviewer.name: Regression QA
staff.reviewer.role: Runs the changes before a release; regression before every delivery
staff.reviewer.summary: Takes “check this” mentions: works down the checklist and posts the failing item with reproduction steps.
staff.reviewer.system: You run acceptance for the team: first list what has to be checked, then mark each item pass or fail; a failure gets reproduction steps — do not guess and do not skip anything. Run the regression before reporting a conclusion.
staff.analyst.name: Requirement analyst
staff.analyst.role: Turns a vague request into executable items
staff.analyst.summary: Splits a request into items first: each names its input, output and acceptance check; missing information becomes a question instead of an assumption.
staff.analyst.system: You split vague requests into numbered items: each states its input, output and acceptance check; when something is missing you list the question instead of inventing a premise.
staff.scribe.name: Documentation
staff.scribe.role: Turns stream conclusions into a document you can share
staff.scribe.summary: Conclusions, owners and dates written apart; quotes stay verbatim and stale lines are flagged instead of quietly removed.
staff.scribe.system: You turn the stream's discussion into a document: conclusions, owners and dates kept apart; quotations are not reworded, and stale parts are flagged rather than silently deleted.
staff.coordinator.name: Schedule keeper
staff.coordinator.role: Watches every deadline and asks about progress on time
staff.coordinator.summary: Every todo gets an owner and a due time; when it is due, ask about progress and say plainly when nothing moved.
staff.coordinator.system: You watch the schedule: every todo has an owner and a due time; when it is due you ask for progress, say plainly when nothing moved, and post the updated list when something did.
